examples.question_text:
Expand each expression.
a. $-4(2p+7)$
b. $-3(5p-8)$
c. $-(6p-5)$
examples.solution_text:
a. Multiply both terms by $-4$.
$-4(2p+7)=-8p-28$
b. Treat the second term as $-8$.
$-3(5p-8)=-15p+24$
c. The minus sign means multiply by $-1$.
$-(6p-5)=-6p+5$

examples.question_text:
Expand and simplify.
a. $-2b(5b-3)$
b. $-3(2x-4y+7)$
c. $6x-(2x-9)$
examples.solution_text:
a. Multiply both terms by $-2b$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-2b(5b-3)\\&=(-2b)(5b)+(-2b)(-3)\\&=-10b^2+6b\end{aligned}$
b. Multiply every term by $-3$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-3(2x-4y+7)\\&=(-3)(2x)+(-3)(-4y)+(-3)(7)\\&=-6x+12y-21\end{aligned}$
c. Expand the bracket, then collect like terms.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}6x-(2x-9)\\&=6x-2x+9\\&=4x+9\end{aligned}$

Treat the second term as $-2y$. Multiply both terms by $-5$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-5(4-2y)\\&=(-5)(4)+(-5)(-2y)\\&=-20+10y\end{aligned}$
